A fast start on the track and the field was led by Coleman through a reputed 7.37 mile! After the 10 laps we moved out on to the road with George leading from Bryan Hawkins and myself, Bob Goodall, McFarlane, and Don Thompson with the French team.
Ash, a new member and a great asset to the Club, won the 120 yards hurdles with Brian Coleman 2nd and H.
236 lined up for the start and Vickers and Hall were seen to be well placed shortly afterwards behind Hardy, Coleman, Hawkins, Poole and others.

Although we just missed a place in the scratch team event, Eric Hall walked exceedingly well to finish in fourth position behind three really first class walkers in Hawkins, Coleman and Poole on a course which is probably the fastest one in the south.

Stan Vickers was 2nd to Coleman who was invincible on the day and Eric Hall produced his best time for the distance. In the remaining events we had little or no interest and our hopes turned to the few numbers left to battle out our cause on Saturday which proved to be an absolute "stinker".
Hardy and Allen of Sheffield quickly took the lead at a fast pace, followed by Stan, Coleman and Hawkins. Allen soon came under the judges ban and was disqualified.

Stan Vickers led from the start, followed by George Coleman and at the mile they were 6 m.56s. and 7 m. 3s. respectively. Although Coleman got within 60 yds. of Stan, he could get no nearer and Stan went on to a meeting record of 8 mls. 120 yds.

Stan kept with Hardy and Coleman in the lead until 8-8½ mls but then dropped 5 yards or so.He recovered again and was with the leaders when they went off course after being misdirected,and lost at least ½ ml.After retracing their steps,they decided to walk back together to the stadium.
Coleman collected a point here for his fourth place and a further two in the shot, which was won by Rasey, our 3rd(!) claim member from Southgate and Barnet.
• Of the favourites: Coleman (South Africa) was 4th, Heino (Finland) 11th, Côte (Canada) 17th, Vogel (USA) 14th, Kyriakidis (Greece) 18th, Kelley (USA) 21st, Yun Bok Suh (Korea) 27th.

Andy Coleman, of Enfield, jumped with 600 to go and was followed by an attentive Newham man in the form of Steve Hepples. Stephen Sharp (another who had returned recently from warm weather training in Portugal) sprinted to cover and passed Hepples but failed to catch Coleman.
James Kelly was content to let Medway’s Mike Coleman take up the pace for three or four laps, sitting at the back of a bunch of four ... and then three ... as the laps ticked away.
